newsitem.title: INDIA: Unit Trust of India drives up Delhi shares.
newsitem.headline: Unit Trust of India drives up Delhi shares.

text.p: Strong buying by domestic financial institutions checked an early decline and helped revive share prices on the Delhi stock Exchange, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index quoted 3.40 points higher at 683.23 at 2.30 p.m.(0900 GMT).
"The domestic financial houses, particularly the Unit Trust of India (UTI), have entered the market to check the constant fall in share values," said Suresh Aggarwal of brokers Jaimata Securities.
Unit Trust of India is the country's largest mutual fund.
Traders said the reprieve was more temporary than permanent in nature as the market is still waiting for the current political scenario to clear up.

The continuing political crisis that has engulfed former Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao, in which he won a temporary respite from arrest on Monday after courts deferred rulings in two criminal cases, also dampened the financial markets.
Deve Gowda's centre-left coalition depends on the support of Congress to survive in parliament against a challenge from the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
Reliance Industries quoted at 185.70, after touching a low of 185.25, though two rupees lower than Monday's close, brokers said.
ITC gained three rupees to quote at 308.50, brokers said.
